title: "I have told you. Now do as you choose." (18.59–18.66)
hook: after seven hundred verses, Krishna hands the decision back to Arjuna
tomorrow: "Abandon all dharmas, come to me alone" (18.66–18.72)

segments.voice: Yesterday: brahmabhuta, the path to Brahman, the whole road in ten verses, and love at the summit. Your line was steady. Did one steady breath come before a reply? Today, the most surprising move in the book. Day two hundred twenty-four.

Imagine the best teacher you ever had spending months with you. Every question answered, every doubt heard, and once, a vision that nearly knocked you over. And then, at the very end, instead of saying, so now you must do this, they close the book and say: I've told you everything. Think it over. Then do what you choose. That's what happens in chapter eighteen. God, in the Gita's own story, doesn't command the final move. He hands it back.
screen: `MONTHS OF ANSWERS.` → `ONE OVERWHELMING VISION.` → `THEN: DO AS YOU CHOOSE.`

segments.voice: It starts with a warning. Verse fifty-nine: if, leaning on your ego, you think, I will not fight, that decision is useless. Your own nature will push you to it. Verse sixty: bound by your own work, born of your nature, you'll do helplessly what you, confused, don't want to do. Then verse sixty-one, a strange picture. The Lord lives in the heart of every being, Arjuna, and by his power moves them all, as if they were mounted on a machine. Verse sixty-two: go to him for refuge with your whole being. By his grace you'll reach the highest peace. And then verse sixty-three. So I have told you this wisdom, more secret than any secret. Reflect on it fully. Then do as you wish. Yathecchasi tatha kuru. As you wish, so do. After all the teaching, all the argument, the vision of chapter eleven, Krishna doesn't force a choice. Many readers, especially modern teachers, find this one of the most striking moments in the book. The Gita's God persuades, shows, loves, and then respects Arjuna enough to let him decide. But he doesn't walk away. Verse sixty-four: hear my highest word once more. You are deeply loved by me. Verse sixty-five repeats a line from chapter nine: keep your mind on me, be devoted to me, and you will come to me. I promise you truly, for you are dear to me. So the handing back isn't cold. It comes wrapped in the plainest statement of love in the whole book. This closes the week: sat, relinquishment, five causes, three kinds, your own dharma, steady, and now this. That's the word today: I have told you. Now do as you choose.
screen: `YOUR NATURE WILL MOVE YOU.` · `THE LORD IN EVERY HEART.` · `REFLECT, THEN DO AS YOU WISH.` · `YOU ARE DEEPLY LOVED.` · then, large: `NOW DO AS YOU CHOOSE.`

segments.voice: Sit, and bring to mind one choice you're facing. Let yourself hear all the advice you've been given about it, from people, from books, from these days. Let it all be said. Then let it go quiet. Now, in the quiet, reflect on it fully, the way verse sixty-three asks. You don't have to decide. Just notice that the choice is yours, and that you can make it without fear. The bell holds the time.
Yathecchasi, as you wish. Gita eighteen, sixty-three: after all the teaching, Krishna says reflect fully, then do as you wish, yathecchasi tatha kuru.
Your line: he hands it back. Today, when you give someone advice, finish the way Krishna does: say what you think, then let them choose. Day two hundred twenty-four.

howItsDone: Hindu teachers often point to Gita 18.63, 'reflect fully, then do as you wish', as a sign that the Gita invites understanding and free choice rather than blind obedience.

fork.setup: you're Krishna. you've taught for seventeen chapters and shown Arjuna your cosmic form. how do you finish?
options: tell him to reflect fully, then do as he wishes.
fork.reveal: reflect fully, then do as you wish (18.63), followed at once by: you are deeply loved by me (18.64).

original.note: Sanskrit: yathecchasi tatha kuru, as you wish, so do; the end of Gita 18.63.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Gita ends with God giving Arjuna an order.
what it means: Krishna teaches fully, then hands the choice back, wrapped in a promise of love.
what a scholar hears: 18.63 'vimrishyaitad asheshena yathecchasi tatha kuru', reflect on this completely and do as you wish; 18.65 repeats 9.34 almost exactly.

notes: All verses paraphrased. The index title "I have told you. Now do as you choose." is itself a paraphrase of 18.63, not a quotation from a public-domain translation; a Keeper may prefer the title without quotation marks.

The index word is cut short ('"I have told you. Now do as you choose."') because it's the title's head; the script keeps it exactly, as the validator requires. The owner may want to fix the index word.
